title: Parental, gestational, and early-life exposure to indoor environmental hazardous factors on allergic rhinitis among preschool children in Urumqi City: a case-control study.
ehr_evidence: Questionnaires were developed for all children in the case group and control group; the questionnaire contents were adapted from the questionnaires used in the CCHH survey study and were slightly revised according to the specific context of Urumqi City.
summary: Case-control study investigating the association between parental, gestational, and early-life indoor environmental exposures and allergic rhinitis in preschool children in Urumqi City, China.
key_findings: Cesarean section was associated with AR (OR = 1.31, 95% CI = 1.02-1.67, p < 0.05).
Father with AR was associated with AR (OR = 2.67, 95% CI = 2.08-3.44, p < 0.05).
Mother with AR was associated with AR (OR = 3.70, 95% CI = 2.88-4.74, p < 0.05).
Mother with asthma was associated with AR (OR = 3.11, 95% CI = 1.18-8.20, p < 0.05).
Newly purchased furniture in parents' residence during pregnancy was associated with AR (OR = 1.49, 95% CI = 1.03-2.14, p < 0.05).
No significant association was found for passive smoking, petkeeping, or indoor dampness in the multivariate model.
captured_features: Parental history of AR and asthma
Living habits (pets, plants, smoking, air conditioning)
population: preschool children in Urumqi City, China (mean age 5.18 years; 404 cases, 1616 controls)
limitations: conservative case definition restricted to physician-diagnosed AR
self-reported exposure subject to recall bias
unmeasured confounding from regional air quality improvements
data_availability_statement: The datasets generated and/or analyzed during the current study are not publicly available due to the data belonging to the School of Public Health of Fudan University but are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.
